texts: Depolarisation of the sinoatrial and atrioventricular nodes depends largely on L-type calcium currents, which makes them slow-response tissues: D.
In the picture, the conductor's baton and the knot move only with the slow, thick glue from the L-shaped cans, not with the fast salt.
Nodal cells rest at about -60 mV, not -90 mV like fast-response tissue, and they conduct far more slowly than the His-Purkinje system below them.
The sinoatrial node lies just under the epicardium where the superior vena cava meets the right atrium, not on the endocardium.
In most people the right coronary artery, not the circumflex, supplies both nodes.
Memory hook: the conductor and the knot run on slow glue from L-shaped cans.
